entries.text:
disjoint union. The occurrence sets are defined recursively by
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \Occ(p)&=\{*\},&
 \Occ(\top)&=\Occ(\bot)=\varnothing,\\
 \Occ(\neg A)&=\Occ(A),&
 \Occ(A\mathbin\star C)&=\Occ(A)\sqcup\Occ(C)

entries.text:
Explicitly, let
$k_A=j_A\circ\pi_1^{A,\bot}:A\wedge\bot\to A\vee\top$.

entries.text:
The product and coproduct equations give the commutative square
\[
\begin{tikzcd}[column sep=large,row sep=large]
 A\wedge\bot\arrow[r,"k_A"]\arrow[d,"n_A^{-1}\wedge1_\bot"']
   &A\vee\top\\
 \neg\neg A\wedge\bot\arrow[r,"k_{\neg\neg A}"']
   &\neg\neg A\vee\top\arrow[u,"n_A\vee1_\top"'].
\end{tikzcd}
\]
entries.assessment: Long route: A∧bot --n_A⁻¹∧1→¬¬A∧bot --k_nnA→¬¬A∨top --n_A∨1→A∨top. Product projection naturality, coproduct injection naturality and n_A∘n_A⁻¹=1 identify it with k_A. Each intermediate type matches.

entries.text:
Precomposition and postcomposition of the zero arrow give a zero
arrow by absorption.

entries.text: \section{Contextual collapse}\label{sec:collapse}
entries.assessment: Heading accurately describes the result: K_A for all A entails thin quotient.
entries.check: Heading accurately describes the result: K_A for all A entails thin quotient.

entries.text:
The distributor produces an arrow that treats two copies of $A$
symmetrically.
entries.assessment: The forthcoming h_A is explicitly constructed from d and bicartesian operations; its relation folds the two tags, and coherence proves symmetry.
entries.check: The forthcoming h_A is explicitly constructed from d and bicartesian operations; its relation folds the two tags, and coherence proves symmetry.

entries.text:
This symmetry converts the contextual equation into
an equation between the projections.
entries.assessment: Accurate roadmap: symmetry yields j_Aπ₁≡j_Aπ₂ first, and the later B=top computation removes the contextual injection without cancellation.

entries.text:
For formulas $A,B$, define
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 u_A^B&=d_{A,B,A}\circ(1_A\wedge\iota_2^{B,A})
       :A\wedge A\longrightarrow(A\wedge B)\vee A,\\
 h_A^B&=[\pi_1^{A,B},1_A]\circ u_A^B:A\wedge A\longrightarrow A.
 \end{aligned}
\]
entries.assessment: 1_A∧ι₂^{B,A}:A∧A→A∧(B∨A); d_{A,B,A} gives (A∧B)∨A; [π₁^{A,B},1_A] maps that coproduct to A. Thus both displayed definitions have exactly their declared endpoints.
entries.check: 1_A∧ι₂^{B,A}:A∧A→A∧(B∨A); d_{A,B,A} gives (A∧B)∨A; [π₁^{A,B},1_A] maps that coproduct to A. Thus both displayed definitions have exactly their declared endpoints.

entries.text: The arrow $h_A^B$ is independent of $B$.
entries.assessment: For B and B′, both h arrows lie in Hom(A∧A,A), and the proof gives the same tagged fold relation independent of both parameters; original-B coherence yields equality.
entries.check: For B and B′, both h arrows lie in Hom(A∧A,A), and the proof gives the same tagged fold relation independent of both parameters; original-B coherence yields equality.

entries.text:
Writing it as $h_A$ and
putting $\tau_A=\langle\pi_2^{A,A},\pi_1^{A,A}\rangle$, one has
$h_A\circ\tau_A=h_A$.
entries.assessment: τ_A is the product symmetry A∧A→A∧A. The pair is well typed from projection definitions, but its explicit signature is absent at introduction. Add it to meet the requested typing convention; no mathematical defect is alleged.
entries.repair: Writing it as $h_A$ and putting $\tau_A=\langle\pi_2^{A,A},\pi_1^{A,A}\rangle:A\wedge A\to A\wedge A$, one has $h_A\circ\tau_A=h_A$.
entries.check: τ_A is the product symmetry A∧A→A∧A. The pair is well typed from projection definitions, but its explicit signature is absent at introduction. Add it to meet the requested typing convention; no mathematical defect is alleged.

entries.text:
The relation of $u_A^B$ sends $(1,x)$ to $(1,(1,x))$ and $(2,x)$
to $(2,x)$ in $\bigl(\Occ(A)\sqcup\Occ(B)\bigr)\sqcup\Occ(A)$.
entries.assessment: Tensor with injection retains first tag A and sends second A into the second disjunction branch; rebracketing d sends them to ((1,(1,x))) and (2,x). No B occurrences receive edges. Domain tags are those of Occ(A)⊔Occ(A).

entries.text:
Copairing with $\pi_1^{A,B}$ and $1_A$ then gives
\[
 Gh_A^B=\{((1,x),x),((2,x),x):x\in\Occ(A)\}.
\]
entries.assessment: Postcomposing u_A^B with the copair [π₁^{A,B},1_A] sends both surviving A blocks to x, giving exactly the displayed union of graphs. The original phrase “Copairing with …” describes the operation loosely: the copair is formed from π₁ and 1_A, then composed with u. State that postcomposition and the copair’s type explicitly. The previous definition already makes the inference mathematically valid; this is operational precision, not a proof gap.

entries.text:
This relation is independent of $B$ and invariant under exchange of
the two source tags.
entries.assessment: The target formula A and source A∧A are independent of B. Swapping the two source tags leaves the two-element-per-x description unchanged, including the empty-occurrence case.
entries.check: The target formula A and source A∧A are independent of B. Swapping the two source tags leaves the two-element-per-x description unchanged, including the empty-occurrence case.

entries.text: Boolean Coherence proves both assertions.
entries.assessment: All comparisons are in B, either h_A^B vs h_A^{B′} or h_A∘τ_A vs h_A. Faithfulness yields the required equalities; none is inferred in the quotient.
entries.check: All comparisons are in B, either h_A^B vs h_A^{B′} or h_A∘τ_A vs h_A. Faithfulness yields the required equalities; none is inferred in the quotient.

entries.text:
Let $\theta$ be a proof congruence on $\B$ such that
\eqref{eq:context} holds modulo $\theta$ for every formula $A$.
entries.assessment: Hypothesis requires K_A for all formulas and a proof congruence only. The proof does not invoke substitution closure, which belonged solely to the preceding proposition.
entries.check: Hypothesis requires K_A for all formulas and a proof congruence only. The proof does not invoke substitution closure, which belonged solely to the preceding proposition.

entries.text: Then $\B/\theta$ is a preorder.
entries.assessment: Conclusion means every parallel hom-set in B/θ has at most one element. The proof derives equal projections for each A and then uses product pairing on arbitrary parallels.
entries.check: Conclusion means every parallel hom-set in B/θ has at most one element. The proof derives equal projections for each A and then uses product pairing on arbitrary parallels.

entries.text: Write $\equiv$ for equality modulo $\theta$.
entries.assessment: Notation is explicitly fixed; equalities in original B continue to be written =, while new quotient equalities use ≡.
entries.check: Notation is explicitly fixed; equalities in original B continue to be written =, while new quotient equalities use ≡.

entries.text:
The quotient retains products and coproducts: their pairing,
copairing, and defining equations pass to equivalence classes.
entries.assessment: Congruence under pairing/copairing makes induced operations well defined. Their β and η identities descend and imply existence and uniqueness of maps from/to the product/coproduct in the quotient. Terminality and initiality also persist because all original maps to/from the constants were already unique.
entries.check: Congruence under pairing/copairing makes induced operations well defined. Their β and η identities descend and imply existence and uniqueness of maps from/to the product/coproduct in the quotient. Terminality and initiality also persist because all original maps to/from the constants were already unique.

entries.assessment: All terms have source A∧A and target A∨top. First equality uses j_A postcomposition through a copair; middle uses K_A inside the first copair component; last is original-B relation equality justified immediately below. u_A^bot is still an existing arrow; no empty hom-set is enlarged.
entries.check: All terms have source A∧A and target A∨top. First equality uses j_A postcomposition through a copair; middle uses K_A inside the first copair component; last is original-B relation equality justified immediately below. u_A^bot is still an existing arrow; no empty hom-set is enlarged.

entries.text:
For the last equality, both occurrence relations discard the first
source tag and send $(2,x)$ to $(1,x)$ in $\Occ(A)\sqcup\varnothing$.
entries.assessment: u_A^bot routes first A into the first source summand of the copair, which zero kills; second A enters j_A and reaches first target tag. j_A∘π₂ has exactly this relation.
entries.check: u_A^bot routes first A into the first source summand of the copair, which zero kills; second A enters j_A and reaches first target tag. j_A∘π₂ has exactly this relation.

entries.text: Thus it is an equation of $\B$ by Boolean Coherence.
entries.assessment: The last equality compares parallel arrows of B before passage to θ; using faithfulness here is noncircular.
entries.check: The last equality compares parallel arrows of B before passage to θ; using faithfulness here is noncircular.

entries.text:
Precomposing \eqref{eq:second-block} with $\tau_A$ and using
$h_A\circ\tau_A=h_A$ yields
\[
 j_A\circ\pi_1^{A,A}\equiv j_A\circ\pi_2^{A,A}.
\]
entries.assessment: Precompose both sides with τ_A:A∧A→A∧A. h_Aτ_A=h_A and π₂τ_A=π₁ give j_Ah_A≡j_Aπ₁; combine with j_Ah_A≡j_Aπ₂ to obtain the displayed equivalence. No cancellation of j_A occurs.
entries.check: Precompose both sides with τ_A:A∧A→A∧A. h_Aτ_A=h_A and π₂τ_A=π₁ give j_Ah_A≡j_Aπ₁; combine with j_Ah_A≡j_Aπ₂ to obtain the displayed equivalence. No cancellation of j_A occurs.

entries.text: Now precompose with $\langle1_A,0_A\rangle:A\to A\wedge A$.
entries.assessment: The pair is well typed because 1_A and 0_A share source A and codomain A; projections of it are 1_A and 0_A.
entries.check: The pair is well typed because 1_A and 0_A share source A and codomain A; projections of it are 1_A and 0_A.

entries.assessment: Both sides have source A and target A∨top. Precomposition gives j_A≡j_A0_A. The first = is the witnessed-zero definition with witness j_A; the last = follows from the next sentence’s original-B coherence argument.
entries.check: Both sides have source A and target A∨top. Precomposition gives j_A≡j_A0_A. The first = is the witnessed-zero definition with witness j_A; the last = follows from the next sentence’s original-B coherence argument.

entries.text:
The last equality holds by coherence, since the composite through
$\top$ has empty occurrence relation.
entries.assessment: ι₂^{A,top}∘!_A factors through top with empty occurrence set. It and j_A0_A are parallel empty-relation arrows in B, so original-B coherence applies.
entries.check: ι₂^{A,top}∘!_A factors through top with empty occurrence set. It and j_A0_A are parallel empty-relation arrows in B, so original-B coherence applies.

entries.text:
The arrows $s=\iota_2^{A,\top}:\top\to A\vee\top$ and
$t=!_{A\vee\top}:A\vee\top\to\top$ are inverse in the quotient.
entries.assessment: s:top→A∨top and t:A∨top→top are explicitly typed; inverse laws are shown in the next three sentences, one already in B and one modulo θ.
entries.check: s:top→A∨top and t:A∨top→top are explicitly typed; inverse laws are shown in the next three sentences, one already in B and one modulo θ.

entries.text: Indeed, $t\circ s=1_\top$ by terminality.
entries.assessment: t∘s:top→top equals 1_top because top is terminal. This holds before quotienting.
entries.check: t∘s:top→top equals 1_top because top is terminal. This holds before quotienting.

entries.text:
Equation
\eqref{eq:terminal-injection} gives
$(s\circ t)\circ\iota_1^{A,\top}\equiv\iota_1^{A,\top}$, and
terminality gives
$(s\circ t)\circ\iota_2^{A,\top}=\iota_2^{A,\top}$.
entries.assessment: On first injection, tι₁=!_A, so stι₁=s!_A≡j_A=ι₁ by the earlier equation. On second injection, ts=1_top, so sts=s=ι₂. The use of ≡ vs = is correct.
entries.check: On first injection, tι₁=!_A, so stι₁=s!_A≡j_A=ι₁ by the earlier equation. On second injection, ts=1_top, so sts=s=ι₂. The use of ≡ vs = is correct.

entries.text: The coproduct property therefore gives $s\circ t\equiv1_{A\vee\top}$.
entries.assessment: In the quotient, st and identity have equal restrictions along both coproduct injections by preceding calculations; uniqueness in the retained coproduct universal property yields equality.
entries.check: In the quotient, st and identity have equal restrictions along both coproduct injections by preceding calculations; uniqueness in the retained coproduct universal property yields equality.

entries.text:
Hence $A\vee\top$, and by coproduct symmetry also $\top\vee A$,
is terminal in the quotient.
entries.assessment: A∨top is isomorphic to terminal top in the quotient, hence terminal. The structural coproduct symmetry top∨A≅A∨top is preserved by the quotient, so top∨A is also terminal.
entries.check: A∨top is isomorphic to terminal top in the quotient, hence terminal. The structural coproduct symmetry top∨A≅A∨top is preserved by the quotient, so top∨A is also terminal.

entries.assessment: ι₂^{top,A} and ι₁^{top,A}∘!_A are parallel A→top∨A. Terminality in the quotient makes them equal. This is not asserted as an original-B equality.
entries.check: ι₂^{top,A} and ι₁^{top,A}∘!_A are parallel A→top∨A. Terminality in the quotient makes them equal. This is not asserted as an original-B equality.

entries.text: Evaluate the same arrow $h_A$ using $B=\top$.
entries.assessment: Independence of B has already been proved as equality in B, so using the top-based expression for the same h_A is justified.
entries.check: Independence of B has already been proved as equality in B, so using the top-based expression for the same h_A is justified.

entries.assessment: Types along expanded route: A∧A --1∧!→A∧top --1∧ι₁→A∧(top∨A) --d→(A∧top)∨A --[π₁,1]→A. Equation(1) shortens the middle two to ι₁^{A∧top,A}; copair β gives π₁^{A,top}; product naturality then gives π₁^{A,A}. First step only modulo θ, following equalities in B.
entries.check: Types along expanded route: A∧A --1∧!→A∧top --1∧ι₁→A∧(top∨A) --d→(A∧top)∨A --[π₁,1]→A. Equation(1) shortens the middle two to ι₁^{A∧top,A}; copair β gives π₁^{A,top}; product naturality then gives π₁^{A,A}. First step only modulo θ, following equalities in B.

entries.text:
Since $h_A$ is invariant under $\tau_A$, this implies
$\pi_1^{A,A}\equiv\pi_2^{A,A}$.
entries.assessment: From h_A≡π₁ and h_Aτ_A=h_A, congruence gives π₁τ_A≡π₁; π₁τ_A=π₂, so projections are equivalent.
entries.check: From h_A≡π₁ and h_Aτ_A=h_A, congruence gives π₁τ_A≡π₁; π₁τ_A=π₂, so projections are equivalent.

entries.text:
For any parallel arrows $f,g:X\to A$, pairing now gives
\[
 f=\pi_1^{A,A}\circ\langle f,g\rangle
   \equiv\pi_2^{A,A}\circ\langle f,g\rangle=g.
\]
entries.assessment: f,g:X→A have a pair X→A∧A. The product β laws identify its composites with π₁ and π₂ as f and g; congruence under precomposition with the pair proves f≡g.
entries.check: f,g:X→A have a pair X→A∧A. The product β laws identify its composites with π₁ and π₂ as f and g; congruence under precomposition with the pair proves f≡g.

entries.text: Thus the quotient is a preorder.
entries.assessment: The preceding argument covers every target A and every parallel pair with any source X, exactly thinness. Hom-sets that were empty remain empty.
entries.check: The preceding argument covers every target A and every parallel pair with any source X, exactly thinness. Hom-sets that were empty remain empty.

entries.text:
Suppose that a substitution congruence $\theta$ on $\B(P)$ identifies
two distinct parallel arrows.
entries.assessment: This begins proof of the main theorem with its sole nontrivial hypothesis: a substitution congruence properly identifying an original pair. Equality itself and totality are already congruences.
entries.check: This begins proof of the main theorem with its sole nontrivial hypothesis: a substitution congruence properly identifying an original pair. Equality itself and totality are already congruences.

entries.text:
Proposition~\ref{prop:all-contexts}
gives \eqref{eq:context} modulo $\theta$ for every formula $A$.
entries.assessment: Correct invocation of the all-contexts proposition under substitution congruence and nontrivial pair hypotheses.
entries.check: Correct invocation of the all-contexts proposition under substitution congruence and nontrivial pair hypotheses.

entries.text: Lemma~\ref{lem:collapse} then makes $\theta$ total.
entries.assessment: The collapse lemma needs only a proof congruence and all K_A, both furnished above. Thin quotient is equivalent to θ containing every parallel pair.
entries.check: The collapse lemma needs only a proof congruence and all K_A, both furnished above. Thin quotient is equivalent to θ containing every parallel pair.

entries.text:
The same argument gives the formulation of maximality in terms of
models used in \cite[\S9.3, p.~194]{DP}.
entries.assessment: Source §9.3 printed p.194 defines maximality by every natural category satisfying a new equation becoming a preorder. The following corollary instantiates this all-interpretations semantics for the zero-identity Boolean signature.
entries.check: Source §9.3 printed p.194 defines maximality by every natural category satisfying a new equation becoming a preorder. The following corollary instantiates this all-interpretations semantics for the zero-identity Boolean signature.

entries.text:
An \emph{interpretation} in
a zero-identity Boolean category $\mathcal C$ assigns an object of
$\mathcal C$ to each propositional variable and interprets the
specified operations; it induces a structure-preserving functor
$\B(P)\to\mathcal C$.
entries.assessment: Interpretation assigns variables to objects and the specified signature to its given operations in C; initial freeness of B(P) yields the covariant functor, sending formulas to their interpretations and terms to arrow interpretations. Relations in the source presentation hold in a zero-identity Boolean category by definition. This is not an arbitrary functor.
entries.check: Interpretation assigns variables to objects and the specified signature to its given operations in C; initial freeness of B(P) yields the covariant functor, sending formulas to their interpretations and terms to arrow interpretations. Relations in the source presentation hold in a zero-identity Boolean category by definition. This is not an arbitrary functor.

entries.text:
Let $P$ be a nonempty set of propositional variables, and let
$f,g:A\to C$ be distinct arrows of $\B(P)$.
entries.assessment: P nonempty is needed later to choose p and assign its interpretation to any object X. Distinctness furnishes a nontrivial kernel-intersection congruence; parallelism ensures equality is typed.
entries.check: P nonempty is needed later to choose p and assign its interpretation to any object X. Distinctness furnishes a nontrivial kernel-intersection congruence; parallelism ensures equality is typed.

entries.text:
If a zero-identity Boolean category $\mathcal C$ satisfies $f=g$
under every interpretation of the propositional variables, then
$\mathcal C$ is a preorder.
entries.assessment: The assumption is every object interpretation, not one interpretation. The proof uses the intersection of all kernels to obtain substitution closure and then interprets a chosen variable by every object; its endpoint is thinness of C.
entries.check: The assumption is every object interpretation, not one interpretation. The proof uses the intersection of all kernels to obtain substitution closure and then interprets a chosen variable by every object; its endpoint is thinness of C.

entries.text:
Declare two parallel arrows of $\B(P)$ equivalent when all their
interpretations in $\mathcal C$ agree.
entries.assessment: For each source hom-set, intersection of equivalence kernels gives an equivalence relation. Each interpretation preserves arrow operations, so the intersection is an operation congruence; underlying morphisms with unequal objects are never compared.
entries.check: For each source hom-set, intersection of equivalence kernels gives an equivalence relation. Each interpretation preserves arrow operations, so the intersection is an operation congruence; underlying morphisms with unequal objects are never compared.

entries.text:
This defines a substitution
congruence: composing an interpretation with $F_\sigma$ is another
interpretation.
entries.assessment: For σ:P→Form(P) and any interpretation H:B(P)→C, H∘F_σ is another interpretation. If H′f=H′g for every H′, then taking H′=H∘F_σ proves all H agree on f[σ],g[σ]. This does not incorrectly assert one fixed interpretation kernel is substitution stable.
entries.check: For σ:P→Form(P) and any interpretation H:B(P)→C, H∘F_σ is another interpretation. If H′f=H′g for every H′, then taking H′=H∘F_σ proves all H agree on f[σ],g[σ]. This does not incorrectly assert one fixed interpretation kernel is substitution stable.

entries.text:
The congruence contains $f=g$, so
Theorem~\ref{thm:main} makes it total.
entries.assessment: The corollary assumption places the specified distinct f,g in the intersection; the main theorem therefore applies to that substitution congruence.
entries.check: The corollary assumption places the specified distinct f,g in the intersection; the main theorem therefore applies to that substitution congruence.

entries.text:
In particular,
$\pi_1^{p,p}=\pi_2^{p,p}$ holds under every interpretation, for any
$p\in P$.
entries.assessment: Totality applies to the two parallel arrows π₁^{p,p},π₂^{p,p}. The definition of the intersection then says every interpretation makes their images equal.
entries.check: Totality applies to the two parallel arrows π₁^{p,p},π₂^{p,p}. The definition of the intersection then says every interpretation makes their images equal.

entries.text: Interpret $p$ as an arbitrary object $X$ of $\mathcal C$.
entries.assessment: Choose p using nonempty P. An assignment exists for each X: send p to X and all other variables to the terminal object of C; freeness yields its interpretation. C is nonempty since it has top.
entries.check: Choose p using nonempty P. An assignment exists for each X: send p to X and all other variables to the terminal object of C; freeness yields its interpretation. C is nonempty since it has top.

entries.text: Its two projections $X\wedge X\to X$ are equal.
entries.assessment: The chosen interpretation preserves the specified product and projections, so the previous interpreted equality is π₁^{X,X}=π₂^{X,X}.
entries.check: The chosen interpretation preserves the specified product and projections, so the previous interpreted equality is π₁^{X,X}=π₂^{X,X}.

entries.text:
Pairing any arrows
$a,b:Y\to X$ with these projections yields $a=b$.
entries.assessment: The mathematical inference is valid, but the phrase “Pairing any arrows … with these projections” conflates forming the pair with composing it with projections. Pair a,b:Y→X to obtain ⟨a,b⟩:Y→X∧X, then compose with the equal projections. This is a local wording ambiguity, not a proof gap.

$\underline0=\varnothing$.

entries.text:
A \emph{formula pattern} on a finite set
of placeholders is a formula in those placeholders.
entries.evidence: Definition uses Form already defined for an arbitrary variable set; constants remain allowed even if the placeholder set is empty.
entries.check: Definition uses Form already defined for an arbitrary variable set; constants remain allowed even if the placeholder set is empty.

entries.text:
Its
\emph{occurrence profile} records the placeholder at each position,
reading positions from left to right.
entries.evidence: A profile records positions rather than collapsing repeated equal placeholders; formal codomain appears immediately below.
entries.check: A profile records positions rather than collapsing repeated equal placeholders; formal codomain appears immediately below.

entries.text:
Let $U=\{p_1,\ldots,p_k\}$ consist of distinct placeholders and let
$M\in\FormulaSet(U)$ have $m$ occurrences.
entries.evidence: Distinct enumerated p_i make each occurrence index uniquely identifiable; unused placeholders are permitted.
entries.check: Distinct enumerated p_i make each occurrence index uniquely identifiable; unused placeholders are permitted.

entries.text:
Its profile is
\[
 o_M:\underline m\longrightarrow\underline k,
 \qquad o_M(r)=i\quad\text{when position $r$ contains $p_i$}.
\]
entries.evidence: Typed o_M: underline(m) -> underline(k); each occurrence has exactly one placeholder index because U is an enumerated set of distinct placeholders. If k=0 then m=0. Display checked.
entries.check: Typed o_M: underline(m) -> underline(k); each occurrence has exactly one placeholder index because U is an enumerated set of distinct placeholders. If k=0 then m=0. Display checked.

entries.text:
For each $i\in\underline k$, choose a set
$Q_i=\{q_{i,1},\ldots,q_{i,\ell_i}\}$ of distinct local placeholders and a
pattern $N_i\in\FormulaSet(Q_i)$ with $n_i$ occurrences.
entries.evidence: Each local finite set is separately enumerated without repetitions; n_i may be zero for closed patterns.
entries.check: Each local finite set is separately enumerated without repetitions; n_i may be zero for closed patterns.

entries.text:
The sets
$Q_i$ are pairwise disjoint.
entries.evidence: This is an explicit permissible hypothesis; the later tagging makes the resulting target labels identifiable.
entries.check: This is an explicit permissible hypothesis; the later tagging makes the resulting target labels identifiable.

entries.text:
Write
$o_i:\underline{n_i}\to\underline{\ell_i}$ for the profile of $N_i$.
entries.evidence: Typed map o_i from occurrence positions to local placeholder indices; no injectivity or surjectivity assumed.
entries.check: Typed map o_i from occurrence positions to local placeholder indices; no injectivity or surjectivity assumed.

entries.text: All these numbers may be zero whenever the displayed maps exist.
entries.evidence: Zero arities/occurrence counts cause no undefined map: an empty placeholder set forces an empty occurrence domain; a positive placeholder set may still have a closed formula with no occurrences.
entries.check: Zero arities/occurrence counts cause no undefined map: an empty placeholder set forces an empty occurrence domain; a positive placeholder set may still have a closed formula with no occurrences.

entries.text:
The occurrences after substitution and the local placeholder indices
form, respectively, the sets
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 D&=\{(r,t):r\in\underline m,\ t\in\underline{n_{o_M(r)}}\},\\
 C&=\{(i,s):i\in\underline k,\ s\in\underline{\ell_i}\}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
entries.evidence: D is a dependent tagged sum indexed by every outer occurrence, with local size n_{o_M(r)}. C is the tagged placeholder-index set, not the set of source occurrences. Both definitions have finite endpoints.
entries.check: D is a dependent tagged sum indexed by every outer occurrence, with local size n_{o_M(r)}. C is the tagged placeholder-index set, not the set of source occurrences. Both definitions have finite endpoints.

entries.text:
Thus $(r,t)$ specifies an occurrence in the copy of $N_{o_M(r)}$
inserted at position $r$ of $M$.
entries.evidence: This restates the dependent-sum coordinates and correctly uses the outer profile o_M(r).
entries.check: This restates the dependent-sum coordinates and correctly uses the outer profile o_M(r).

entries.text:
The pair $(i,s)$ specifies a local
placeholder of $N_i$.
entries.evidence: Membership in C guarantees i in underline(k) and s in underline(l_i). A placeholder may be unused in N_i; the claim does not assert it occurs.
entries.check: Membership in C guarantees i in underline(k) and s in underline(l_i). A placeholder may be unused in N_i; the claim does not assert it occurs.

entries.text:
Define the injections
\[
 a_r:\underline{n_{o_M(r)}}\longrightarrow D,\quad a_r(t)=(r,t),
 \qquad
 b_i:\underline{\ell_i}\longrightarrow C,\quad b_i(s)=(i,s).
\]
entries.evidence: a_r and b_i are injective by equality of ordered pairs. Empty-domain injections are still defined. Each target is exactly D or C as declared.
entries.check: a_r and b_i are injective by equality of ordered pairs. Empty-domain injections are still defined. Each target is exactly D or C as declared.

entries.evidence: Both paths have domain underline(n_{o_M(r)}) and codomain C. Existence: gamma(r,t)=(o_M(r),o_{o_M(r)}(t)); inner profile has the required codomain. Uniqueness: each (r,t) lies in exactly one a_r image. If D is empty there is exactly one map D->C.
entries.check: Both paths have domain underline(n_{o_M(r)}) and codomain C. Existence: gamma(r,t)=(o_M(r),o_{o_M(r)}(t)); inner profile has the required codomain. Uniqueness: each (r,t) lies in exactly one a_r image. If D is empty there is exactly one map D->C.

entries.text:
The square says that an occurrence inside one inserted copy is labelled
by that pattern's profile and then placed in the corresponding target
block.
entries.evidence: Lower path computes the local profile then injects into the target block o_M(r); upper path is gamma restricted to the r-th source block.
entries.check: Lower path computes the local profile then injects into the target block o_M(r); upper path is gamma restricted to the r-th source block.

entries.text:
Since $D$ is the disjoint union of its source blocks, these
squares determine $\gamma$ on every element.
entries.evidence: Disjoint-union coverage yields elementwise uniqueness; no unproved categorical coherence is used.
entries.check: Disjoint-union coverage yields elementwise uniqueness; no unproved categorical coherence is used.

entries.text:
Explicitly,
\[
 \gamma(r,t)=\bigl(o_M(r),o_{o_M(r)}(t)\bigr).
\]
entries.evidence: gamma(r,t) is well typed because o_{o_M(r)}(t) lies in underline(l_{o_M(r)}); repeated o_M values keep different source tags.
entries.check: gamma(r,t) is well typed because o_{o_M(r)}(t) lies in underline(l_{o_M(r)}); repeated o_M values keep different source tags.

entries.text:
Define the block projections $p_D:D\to\underline m$ and
$p_C:C\to\underline k$ by $p_D(r,t)=r$ and $p_C(i,s)=i$.
entries.evidence: Both maps are total projections from their dependent tagged sums; values lie in the specified finite ordinals.
entries.check: Both maps are total projections from their dependent tagged sums; values lie in the specified finite ordinals.

entries.evidence: Both paths D->underline(k) evaluate to o_M(r); the diagram expresses a commuting square of functions, without a pullback claim.
entries.check: Both paths D->underline(k) evaluate to o_M(r); the diagram expresses a commuting square of functions, without a pullback claim.

entries.text: Both routes send $(r,t)$ to $o_M(r)$.
entries.evidence: Direct evaluation: p_C(gamma(r,t))=o_M(r)=o_M(p_D(r,t)).
entries.check: Direct evaluation: p_C(gamma(r,t))=o_M(r)=o_M(p_D(r,t)).

entries.text:
This square records which
inserted pattern is used; square~\eqref{eq:app-fibre} specifies the
map within each such block.
entries.evidence: The outer square only fixes target tags; the fibre squares also fix local values. The text distinguishes these two amounts of information.
entries.check: The outer square only fixes target tags; the fibre squares also fix local values. The text distinguishes these two amounts of information.

entries.text:
Repeated values of $o_M$ give separate
source blocks, one for each occurrence of the corresponding outer
placeholder.
entries.evidence: The first coordinate of D is occurrence index r, so equal o_M values do not identify different source blocks.
entries.check: The first coordinate of D is occurrence index r, so equal o_M values do not identify different source blocks.

entries.text:
To identify this construction with actual pattern substitution,
replace each $q_{i,s}$ in $N_i$ by $(i,s)$ and denote the resulting
pattern over $C$ by $\widetilde N_i$.
entries.evidence: Each local placeholder q_{i,s} has unique s, so renaming to (i,s) is well defined; the new labels are in C.
entries.check: Each local placeholder q_{i,s} has unique s, so renaming to (i,s) is well defined; the new labels are in C.

entries.text:
Let
$\Phi_0:U\to\FormulaSet(C)$ be given by $\Phi_0(p_i)=\widetilde N_i$.
entries.evidence: p_i are distinct and exhaust U, so this defines a total substitution U->Form(C).
entries.check: p_i are distinct and exhaust U, so this defines a total substitution U->Form(C).

entries.text: Every occurrence of $M[\Phi_0]$ has unique coordinates $(r,t)\in D$.
entries.evidence: Structural recursion on M: a variable p_i contributes a copy of N_i, constants contribute none, connectives concatenate tags, and negation leaves occurrence sets unchanged. This gives both uniqueness and coverage.
entries.check: Structural recursion on M: a variable p_i contributes a copy of N_i, constants contribute none, connectives concatenate tags, and negation leaves occurrence sets unchanged. This gives both uniqueness and coverage.

entries.evidence: chi is the structural-recursion bijection just described. Both square paths Occ(M[Phi_0])->C yield the placeholder (o_M(r),o_{o_M(r)}(t)); bottom map is identity_C. Empty domains are harmless.
entries.check: chi is the structural-recursion bijection just described. Both square paths Occ(M[Phi_0])->C yield the placeholder (o_M(r),o_{o_M(r)}(t)); bottom map is identity_C. Empty domains are harmless.

entries.text:
Indeed, the occurrence with coordinates $(r,t)$ contains precisely
the placeholder $\bigl(o_M(r),o_{o_M(r)}(t)\bigr)$.
entries.evidence: The outer slot picks N_{o_M(r)}, whose local t-th occurrence has index o_{o_M(r)}(t); target renaming appends the selected pattern index.

entries.text:
The block encodings are the bijections
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \theta_D:D&\longrightarrow\underline{s_m},
       &\theta_D(r,t)&=s_{r-1}+t,\\
 \theta_C:C&\longrightarrow\underline{t_k},
       &\theta_C(i,s)&=t_{i-1}+s.
 \end{aligned}
\]
entries.evidence: Each map adds the cumulative size of preceding blocks. For x in the source ordinal, the unique r satisfying s_{r-1}<x<=s_r determines t=x-s_{r-1}; the analogous inverse gives target coordinates. Empty blocks cannot contain a position; when the total is zero the unique empty function is bijective.

and local position visible; the bottom route uses a single position

entries.text:
For formulas $A,B,C$, equation~\eqref{eq:first-injection} is the
commutative triangle
\[
\begin{tikzcd}[column sep=large,row sep=large]
 A\wedge B
   \arrow[r,"1_A\wedge\iota_1^{B,C}"]
   \arrow[dr,"{\iota_1^{A\wedge B,C}}"']
   &A\wedge(B\vee C)\arrow[d,"d_{A,B,C}"]\\
   &(A\wedge B)\vee C.
\end{tikzcd}
\]

entries.text: \paragraph{The zero identity.}
entries.check: Heading identifies the endomorphism defined by equation (2).

entries.text:
For a formula $A$, equation~\eqref{eq:zero-identity} is expressed by
the commutative diagram
\[
\begin{tikzcd}[column sep=large,row sep=large]
 A\arrow[r,"{\langle1_A,!_A\rangle}"]\arrow[d,"0_A"']
   &A\wedge\top\arrow[r,"1_A\wedge\eta_A"]
   &A\wedge(\neg A\vee A)\arrow[d,"d_{A,\neg A,A}"]\\
 A
   &\bot\vee A\arrow[l,"{[\kappa_A,1_A]}"']
   &(A\wedge\neg A)\vee A\arrow[l,"\epsilon_A\vee1_A"'].
\end{tikzcd}
\]
entries.check: All five composite arrows are typed in sequence: A→A∧top→A∧(neg A∨A)→(A∧neg A)∨A→bot∨A→A. The separate arrow 0_A:A→A is parallel to that path. The diagram states equation (2), which DP calls (0ηε), printed p317.

entries.text: The path across the top, down the right side, and back along the bottom is the five-arrow composite in~\eqref{eq:zero-identity}.
entries.check: Reading the diagram in the stated order yields pairing, 1∧eta, d, epsilon∨1, copairing. Algebraic composition in (2) lists those five in reverse evaluation order, as §2 explicitly stipulates.

entries.text: Its first arrow pairs $1_A:A\to A$ with $!_A:A\to\top$; its last arrow copairs $\kappa_A:\bot\to A$ with $1_A:A\to A$.
entries.check: Both pairing components share domain A, giving A→A∧top; both copairing components share codomain A, giving bot∨A→A. Operational first/last refer to the immediately preceding path description.

entries.text: The arrows between them use $\eta_A:\top\to\neg A\vee A$ and $\epsilon_A:A\wedge\neg A\to\bot$, together with the distributor.
entries.check: The three interior arrows are their indicated tensors with identity and d_{A,neg A,A}; the supplied types ensure all intermediate composites exist.

entries.text: \paragraph{The zero law.}
entries.check: Heading identifies equation (3), the zero law.

entries.text:
For any parallel arrows $f,g:A\to C$,
equation~\eqref{eq:zero-law} is the commutative square
\[
\begin{tikzcd}[column sep=large,row sep=large]
 A\arrow[r,"0_A"]\arrow[d,"g"']&A\arrow[d,"f"]\\
 C\arrow[r,"0_C"']&C.
\end{tikzcd}
\]
entries.check: Square endpoints: top 0_A:A→A, right f:A→C, left g:A→C, bottom 0_C:C→C. Both paths have type A→C. Its commutativity is precisely f∘0_A=0_C∘g; no equality of f and g is assumed.

entries.text: The upper-right path is $f\circ0_A:A\to C$, and the lower-left path is $0_C\circ g:A\to C$.
entries.check: Composite order agrees with the declared convention (rightmost first) and with the actual drawn paths.

entries.text: The arrows $f$ and $g$ need not be equal.
entries.check: Equation (3) quantifies over independent parallel arrows. For A=p∧p and C=p, distinct projections supply an actual unequal example in B, so this is more than a vacuous observation.
